citations.quote: Loss of the CDKN2A tumor‑suppressor locus (p16INK4a) is observed in a subset of lung adenocarcinomas

candidates.description: Homozygous deletion of the CDKN2A tumor-suppressor locus (p16INK4a).
candidates.extraction_instruction: Search the 'Genomic Findings' or 'Molecular Pathology' sections for mentions of CDKN2A homozygous loss or deletion.
candidates.measurement_definition: Presence is defined by a genomic profiling report indicating 'homozygous loss' or 'homozygous deletion' of the CDKN2A gene/locus. Absence is the lack of such a finding in the genomic report.
candidates.name: CDKN2A homozygous loss
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the clinical significance varies by the specific exons deleted (e.g., exons 1-2).

candidates.description: Homozygous loss of the STK11 gene.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Check the genomic findings table for STK11 status, specifically looking for 'Homozygous deletion'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Presence is defined by a genomic profiling report identifying a 'Homozygous deletion' of STK11. Absence is the lack of such a finding.
candidates.name: STK11 homozygous deletion
candidates.uncertainty: The frequency of this alteration across the specific cohort being analyzed.

limitations: The evidence is derived from a small number of genomic reports.
The analysis lacks a comparison group (patients without these alterations) within the provided snippets to quantify the shift in retrieval signal.
summary: The evidence identifies specific genomic tumor-suppressor losses (CDKN2A and STK11) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients, which are noted in genomic reports as being associated with more aggressive disease or resistance to specific immunotherapies.
